nodes.description: Gravid female pinworms actively migrate to the anal canal at night, leave the anus, and attach eggs to perianal tissue with an adhesive matrix.
nodes.id: Nocturnal Female Migration and Perianal Oviposition

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: Oviposition occurs primarily while the host is resting, i.e., predominantly at night while they sleep. It involves the females leaving the anus and fixing their eggs to tissue in the perianal area with an adhesive matrix.

nodes.description: Scratching the itchy perianal region can produce excoriation with bacterial superinfection, anal dermatitis, perianal folliculitis, or abscess.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: Scratching in the perianal region can cause ulceration (excoriation) that shows a tendency toward bacterial superinfection. Anal dermatitis, perianal folliculitis, or ischiorectal abscess may develop.

nodes.description: Perianal itching is the main and characteristic symptom and is most prominent at night during female worm migration and egg deposition.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: The main symptom of infection is pronounced (peri-)anal pruritus, which occurs primarily at nighttime while the affected individual sleeps.

nodes.description: Pyrantel pamoate and pyrvinium embonate are approved adulticidal alternatives to benzimidazoles; like other enterobiasis drug regimens they require repeat dosing to prevent recurrence from eggs that survive the first dose.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: The approved antihelminthic agents are mebendazole, pyrantel embonate, and pyrvinium embonate

nodes.description: Perianal scratching ruptures migrating females and moves adhesive eggs to hands, fingernails, underwear, bedding, and nearby surfaces, allowing anus-finger-mouth autoinfection and contact spread to maintain the chain of infection.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: The disintegration of the worm cuticle caused by fingers and finger nails leads to a massive release and spreading of eggs into underwear and the surrounding area. The contaminated hands of the host play an important role in maintaining the chain of infection (autoinfection)

nodes.description: Nocturnal itch can disrupt sleep in symptomatic infection.

evidence.reference_title: Pinworm (Enterobius vermicularis) in children and adults: a practice-oriented narrative review and household-school algorithm.
evidence.snippet: Classic features include nocturnal perianal pruritus, sleep disturbance, and occasionally visible small white worms near the anus or in stool ( 3 ).

nodes.description: Treating the index patient and household members on the same day, with a repeat dose 14 days later, interrupts reinfection from asymptomatic contacts and newly maturing larvae.

evidence.reference_title: Pinworm (Enterobius vermicularis) in children and adults: a practice-oriented narrative review and household-school algorithm.
evidence.snippet: In practice, three agents are used interchangeably with high clinical success when the schedule is respected and reinfection is prevented. Mebendazole is typically given as 100 mg orally once and repeated 2 weeks later; pyrantel pamoate is dosed at 11 mg/kg (to a maximum of 1 g) with the same two-week repetition and, in many settings, is available over the counter; albendazole is administered as 400 mg orally once on an empty stomach and repeated on Day 14 ( 3 ).

evidence.reference_title: Pinworm (Enterobius vermicularis) in children and adults: a practice-oriented narrative review and household-school algorithm.
evidence.snippet: The index case and all household members should be treated on the same day, regardless of symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: In the case of chronic recurrent infection, simultaneously treating all (including asymptomatic) members of a household (parents, siblings, grandparents, fellow occupants) has proved a successful approach.

nodes.description: Mebendazole or albendazole binds parasite beta-tubulin, inhibits tubulin polymerization, and depletes worm glycogen reserves. Both agents are adulticidal and ovicidal; standard therapy repeats a single dose to clear larvae emerging after the first dose.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: Only the two benzimidazole derivates, mebendazole and albendazole, are both adulticidal and ovicidal and are therefore considered to be the most effective drugs.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Pinworm Infection.
evidence.snippet: The anthelmintic efficacy of benzimidazole is based on binding to ß-tubulin, which inhibits tubulin polymerization
